ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, there is a circle with a point $O$ on the side $BC$ of $\triangle ABC$ as the center. This circle goes through points $A$ and $B$ and intersects with side $BC$ at point $E$. $DO \perp BE$ at point $O$, and $AD$ is connected intersecting $BC$ at $F$, given $AC=FC$. If $\angle ADB= 60^\circ$ and $BD=1$, calculate the area of the shaded part (leave the result in radical form).
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $BO=DO$, and $BD=1$, $\angle DOB=90^\circ$\\
Therefore, in $\triangle BOD$ right at $O$, by the Pythagorean theorem $BO^2+OD^2=BD^2$\\
Thus, we find $BO=DO=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$\\
That is, the radius of the circle $O$ is $\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$\\
Since $\angle ADB=60^\circ$\\
Therefore $\angle AOB=2\angle ADB=120^\circ$\\
Therefore $\angle AOC=180^\circ-\angle AOB=60^\circ$\\
Since $OA\perp AC$\\
Therefore $\angle OAC=90^\circ$\\
Therefore, in $\triangle OAC$ right at $O$, $\tan AOC=\tan 60^\circ=\frac{AC}{OA}=\sqrt{3}$．\\
Since $OA=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$\\
Therefore $AC=\sqrt{3}OA=\frac{\sqrt{6}}{2}$\\
Therefore, the area of $\triangle OAC=\frac{1}{2}OA\cdot AC=\frac{1}{2}\times \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\times \frac{\sqrt{6}}{2}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}$, and the area of the sector $OAE=\frac{60^\circ\pi (\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})^2}{360^\circ}=\frac{\pi }{12}$\\
Therefore, the area of the shaded region $=S_{\triangle OAC}-S_{\text{sector }OAE}=\boxed{\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}-\frac{\pi }{12}}$.

method.method_draft: Coordinate/analytic route deriving C from AC=FC. Read the diagram to set coordinates with O=(0,0), BC as the x-axis, B=(-r,0), E=(r,0), D=(0,-r), and A in the upper-right part of the circle. From BD=1 and B,D on the circle with OB⊥OD, get r√2=1, so r=√2/2. From ∠ADB=60° and the inscribed-angle theorem, ∠AOB=120°; since OB points along the negative x-axis, OA makes a 60° angle with the positive x-axis, so A=(r/2, √3r/2). Find F as the x-intercept of line AD; this gives F=((2−√3)r,0). Let C=(c,0) with c>r. Use the textual condition AC=FC: sqrt((c−r/2)^2+(√3r/2)^2)=c−(2−√3)r. Solve to get c=2r. Then the shaded region is triangle AOC minus sector AOE. The triangle area can be computed directly from coordinates as 1/2·OC·height from A = 1/2·(2r)·(√3r/2)=√3r²/2=√3/4. method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中圆心为 O，O 在水平线 BC 上；B 在圆的左端，E 在圆与 BC 的右交点，D 在 O 的正下方且在圆上，OD 垂直于 BE。A 在圆的右上方，线段 AC 与水平线 BC 形成三角形 ABC，AD 与 BC 相交于 F。阴影区域位于 AC、BC 和圆弧 AE 之间。

推理：按坐标法设 O=(0,0)，BC 为 x 轴，圆半径为 r，则 B=(-r,0)，E=(r,0)，D=(0,-r)。因为 BD=1，所以 BD=\sqrt{r^2+r^2}=r\sqrt2=1，得 r=\frac{\sqrt2}{2}。由 \angle ADB=60^\circ，根据圆周角定理，\angle AOB=120^\circ。由于 OB 指向负 x 轴，所以 OA 与正 x 轴成 60^\circ，因此 A=(\frac r2,\frac{\sqrt3 r}{2})。直线 AD 过 A(\frac r2,\frac{\sqrt3 r}{2}) 和 D(0,-r)，求其 x 轴交点 F，可得 F=((2-\sqrt3)r,0)。设 C=(c,0)，且 c>r。由题设 AC=FC，有 \sqrt{(c-\frac r2)^2+(\frac{\sqrt3 r}{2})^2}=c-(2-\sqrt3)r。两边平方并化简得 c=2r。阴影面积等于三角形 AOC 的面积减去扇形 AOE 的面积。三角形 AOC 的面积为 \frac12\cdot OC\cdot A到x轴的高=\frac12\cdot 2r\cdot \frac{\sqrt3 r}{2}=\frac{\sqrt3 r^2}{2}=\frac{\sqrt3}{4}。扇形 AOE 的圆心角为 60^\circ，面积为 \frac{60}{360}\pi r^2=\frac{\pi}{6}\cdot\frac12=\frac{\pi}{12}。所以阴影面积为 \frac{\sqrt3}{4}-\frac{\pi}{12}。

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, there is a circle with a point $O$ on the side $BC$ of $\triangle ABC$ as the center. This circle goes through points $A$ and $B$ and intersects with side $BC$ at point $E$. $DO \perp BE$ at point $O$, and $AD$ is connected intersecting $BC$ at $F$, given $AC=FC$. If $\angle ADB= 60^\circ$ and $BD=1$, calculate the area of the shaded part (leave the result in radical form).
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $BO=DO$, and $BD=1$, $\angle DOB=90^\circ$\\
Therefore, in $\triangle BOD$ right at $O$, by the Pythagorean theorem $BO^2+OD^2=BD^2$\\
Thus, we find $BO=DO=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$\\
That is, the radius of the circle $O$ is $\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$\\
Since $\angle ADB=60^\circ$\\
Therefore $\angle AOB=2\angle ADB=120^\circ$\\
Therefore $\angle AOC=180^\circ-\angle AOB=60^\circ$\\
Since $OA\perp AC$\\
Therefore $\angle OAC=90^\circ$\\
Therefore, in $\triangle OAC$ right at $O$, $\tan AOC=\tan 60^\circ=\frac{AC}{OA}=\sqrt{3}$.\\
Since $OA=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$\\
Therefore $AC=\sqrt{3}OA=\frac{\sqrt{6}}{2}$\\
Therefore, the area of $\triangle OAC=\frac{1}{2}OA\cdot AC=\frac{1}{2}\times \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\times \frac{\sqrt{6}}{2}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}$, and the area of the sector $OAE=\frac{60^\circ\pi (\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})^2}{360^\circ}=\frac{\pi }{12}$\\
Therefore, the area of the shaded region $=S_{\triangle OAC}-S_{\text{sector }OAE}=\boxed{\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}-\frac{\pi }{12}}$
raw_record.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, B, O, F, E, C are on the same horizontal straight line, O is the center of the circle, the circle passes through A, B, and intersects BC on the right side at E; D is directly below O and on the circle, OD is perpendicular to the horizontal line BE; the line connecting A, D intersects BC at F; AC is the side extending from A to the right to C, and the figure shows that AC is tangent to the circle at A, so OA is perpendicular to AC. The shaded part is inside triangle AOC and outside arc AE, that is, it can be regarded as triangle AOC minus sector OAE. Reasoning: Because B, D are both on the circle with O as the center, OB=OD=r. Also because OD⊥BE, and B, O, E are collinear, ∠BOD=90°. In the right isosceles triangle BOD, BD=1, therefore r^2+r^2=1^2, obtaining r=OB=OD=√2/2. It is known that ∠ADB=60°, it is an inscribed angle, and the corresponding central angle ∠AOB=2×60°=120°. Since OB and OC are on the same straight line and in opposite directions, ∠AOC=180°−120°=60°; E is also in the direction of OC, therefore ∠AOE=60°. Also by the tangent property OA⊥AC, so triangle AOC is right-angled at A, and ∠AOC=60°. Thus AC=OA·tan60°=(√2/2)·√3=√6/2. The area of triangle AOC is 1/2·OA·AC=1/2·(√2/2)·(√6/2)=√3/4. The area of sector OAE is (60°/360°)·πr^2=1/6·π·(√2/2)^2=π/12. Therefore the shaded area is √3/4−π/12.
